To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) surgery is not beneficial for adult patients with diffuse low grade gliomas, (2) the evidence for a role in adult patients with high grade glioma is inconclusive, (3) radiotherapy is not beneficial for patients with low grade diffuse gliomas and (4) radiotherapy might have some benefit in adult patients with anaplastic gliomas.

(1) there is no conclusive evidence that early resection improves survival in adult patients with gliomas, and (2) there is no convincing evidence that the timing of intervention affects the risk of malignant transformation.

(a) the role of surgery in adult patients with diffuse low grade glioma remains uncertain, (b) the value of radiotherapy remains to be determined and (c) the role of chemotherapy in adult patients with low grade diffuse gliomas is limited to the subgroup of patients with 1p/19q co deletion.
